summary: Round r1 (restricted network). For Q1 (which basin-level agreements affect hydropower development rights) the primary texts of the Nepal-India Kosi Agreement (1954, revised 1966), Gandak Agreement (1959, revised 1964) and Mahakali Treaty (1996) were located in official or treaty repositories (Nepal MoEWRI, India Ministry of Jal Shakti, PCA, FAOLEX, CommonLII), together with the Nepal-India Power Trade Agreement (2014) and India's unilateral Guidelines for Import/Export (Cross Border) of Electricity (2018) and 2021 Procedure, which condition export-oriented hydropower. No primary instrument for Nepal-China data sharing was located; only news pointers following the reported late-August 2026 Gyirong/Rasuwa event. The basin_agreement_table (ten rows) lists provisions to extract and the relevance of each to hydropower rights; provision-level content is pending until texts are downloaded and read. No empirical values are involved beyond dates, which are to be confirmed from the texts.

findings.claim: Q1: Basin agreements affecting hydropower development rights - the Kosi (1954/1966), Gandak (1959/1964) and Mahakali (1996) instruments with India are the water-allocation agreements; the PTA (2014) and India's cross-border electricity guidelines (2018/2021) govern market access. Provision-level analysis pending retrieval of texts.
findings.note: Leads 25B-L01 to 25B-L13; download, hash and extract clause text in r2.

findings.claim: Whether any Nepal-China instrument governs flood-season hydrological data sharing or glacial-lake monitoring in the Koshi and Trishuli headwaters.
findings.note: Only news pointers (25B-L20, L21). Require MoFA treaty register, DHM, and Chinese Embassy in Nepal/MFA primary statements.

findings.claim: Current implementation status of Pancheshwar (DPR, Pancheshwar Development Authority) and Sapta Koshi High Dam studies.
findings.note: Need JCWR/PDA meeting minutes or joint statements (MoFA, MoEWRI, MEA India).

findings.claim: Downstream India-Bangladesh Ganges treaty term and renewal status, and Nepal-India-Bangladesh power trade arrangements.

Agreement relevance is classified as (a) water allocation/works rights, (b) electricity market access, (c) data sharing/hazard governance; hydropower development rights are affected by (a) and (b) directly and by (c) through risk and cost.

Treaty texts hosted by the counterpart government or by FAOLEX/PCA are treated as primary texts; Nepal-hosted versions (MoEWRI, GIWMS) take precedence where available, and textual differences between copies are recorded, not resolved silently.

data_gaps: No downloads possible in r1; provision-level content pending.
Nepal-China water or hydrological data-sharing instrument: none located.
JCWR / JCIFM / Pancheshwar Development Authority meeting records not located.
Nepal-India long-term power trade understanding (reported 2024) and trilateral Nepal-India-Bangladesh power sale arrangement not located as primary texts.
India-Bangladesh Ganges Water Sharing Treaty text and renewal status not located.
WECS basin plans and National Water Resources Policy text not located.
UN Treaty Collection status for the 1997 Watercourses Convention not located.
Web search budget exhausted in r1; r2 must continue location work.

assumptions.text: Dates given in basin_agreement_table are identifiers from located document titles and are to be confirmed from the texts on retrieval.

India's unilateral cross-border electricity rules are included as a de facto basin-level constraint because they determine market access for Nepali hydropower even though they are not bilateral agreements.
Analytical sources (ISET-Nepal, JVS, MP-IDSA, academic papers) are used to identify contested clauses only; clause content is taken from treaty texts.

challenges.text: Please confirm whether 17E holds MoFA/MEA joint-statement records for JCWR, PDA and power-trade mechanisms; 25B needs them to set implementation status.

Hydropower export scenarios should treat India's cross-border electricity guidelines (ownership/eligibility conditions) as a binding constraint parameter until the text is retrieved; do not assume open access to the Indian market.
SPOF 'India as sole electricity market' should cite BA-04 and BA-05 rows once texts are retrieved; data-sharing gap with China (BA-06) is an additional hazard-governance SPOF candidate for EXP-20.
Source catalog lacks ids for MoEWRI, WECS, FAOLEX/treaty repositories and UN Treaty Collection; suggest adding them (mofa_nepal used as proxy for treaty texts).

uncertainty: Moderate for identification of instruments (texts located in official or treaty repositories); high for implementation status and for Nepal-China arrangements, where only news pointers exist. Clause interpretation is contested between Nepali and Indian analyses; both readings will be recorded.
